pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disseram: "Os discípulos de João jejuam com frequência e fazem orações, e os discípulos dos fariseus também. Mas os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} vivem comendo e bebendo."
pt.R: Eles disseram a Jesus: "Os discípulos de João jejuam muitas vezes, quer dizer, ficam sem comer por um tempo. Eles também fazem orações. Os discípulos dos fariseus fazem o mesmo. Mas os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos comem e bebem!"

am.L: እነርሱም አሉት፦ «የዮሐንስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ብዙ ጊዜ ይጾማሉ፤ ጸሎትም ያደርሳሉ፤ የፈሪሳውያንም [ደቀ መዛሙርት] እንዲሁ፤ የአንተ ግን ይበላሉ፤ ይጠጣሉም።»
am.B: ከዚያም እንዲህ አሉት፦ «የዮሐንስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ዘወትር ይጾማሉ፤ ጸሎትም ያደርሳሉ፤ የፈሪሳውያን ደቀ መዛሙርትም እንዲሁ ያደርጋሉ። ደቀ መዛሙርትህ ግን ዘወትር ይበላሉ፤ ይጠጣሉም።»
am.R: እነርሱም ኢየሱስን እንዲህ አሉት፦ «የዮሐንስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ብዙ ጊዜ ይጾማሉ፤ ይህም ማለት ምግብ ሳይበሉ ይቆያሉ። ይጸልያሉም። የፈሪሳውያን ደቀ መዛሙርትም እንዲሁ ያደርጋሉ። ደቀ መዛሙርትህ ግን ይበላሉ፤ ይጠጣሉም!»

ru.L: Они же сказали {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Ученики Иоанна постятся часто и совершают молитвы, так же и [ученики] фарисеев, а {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} едят и пьют.»
ru.B: Тогда они сказали {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Ученики Иоанна часто постятся и молятся, и ученики фарисеев тоже. А {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} едят и пьют.»
ru.R: Они сказали Иисусу: «Ученики Иоанна часто постятся, то есть ничего не едят. Они также молятся. Ученики фарисеев поступают так же. А {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} ученики едят и пьют!»

uk.L: Вони ж сказали {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Учні Іванові часто постять і моляться, так само й [учні] фарисеїв, а {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} їдять і пʼють.»

ja.L: すると彼らはイエスに言った。「ヨハネの弟子たちはしばしば断食し、祈りをささげている。ファリサイ派の人々の[弟子たち]も同じである。しかし、あなたの[弟子たち]は食べたり飲んだりしている。」
ja.B: そこで彼らはイエスに言った。「ヨハネの弟子たちはたびたび断食し、祈りをささげている。ファリサイ派の弟子たちも同じだ。ところが、あなたの弟子たちは食べたり飲んだりしてばかりいる。」
ja.R: その人たちはイエスに言いました。「ヨハネの弟子たちは、よく断食をしている。断食とは、しばらく食べ物を口にしないことだ。また、祈りもささげている。ファリサイ派の人々の弟子たちも同じだ。それなのに、あなたの弟子たちは食べたり飲んだりしている。」

decisions.choice: a statement: they said to him, "John's disciples fast", the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a question: "Why do John's disciples fast ...?", the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have a statement. Many later ones add "why", making it a question, as in Mark 2:18. The challenge is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they: the Pharisees and their scribes of 5:30
decisions.reason: Luke goes on with the same conversation at Levi's feast.

decisions.choice: fast: go without food for a time, as part of prayer or mourning
decisions.reason: The law set one day of fasting a year, the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Many devout Jews fasted more; a Pharisee in one of Jesus's stories fasts twice a week (18:12).

decisions.choice: make prayers: pray regularly, perhaps at set times
decisions.reason: John taught his disciples a way to pray (11:1).

decisions.choice: which means they go without food
decisions.reason: Readable explains fasting.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees speak to Jesus in 합쇼체, with "선생님의" for "yours"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:18 and 2:24 in Korean: their question is critical but not openly hostile.

decisions.choice: "금식" at every level, explained once (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 2:18 in Korean.

decisions.choice: the speakers call Jesus "ông", with no setting span
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says they are the Pharisees and their scribes of 5:30. In Mark 2:18 the questioners are not named as opponents and say "Thầy"; here Vietnamese gives them the opponents' "ông", which takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "kiêng ăn" for fasting
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:18: "ăn chay" today means eating no meat; Readable explains "kiêng ăn" once with "nhịn ăn".

ja.L: するとイエスは彼らに言われた。「花婿が彼らと共にいる間に、婚礼の部屋の子らを断食させることが、あなたがたにできるだろうか？
ja.B: イエスは彼らにお答えになった。「花婿がまだ一緒にいるのに、婚礼の客たちに断食させることができるだろうか？
ja.R: イエスは答えられました。「結婚式では、花婿が一緒にいる間、招かれた客たちは食事をしないでいたりはしない。あなたたちも、客たちにそんなことはさせられないだろう。

decisions.choice: sons of the bridal chamber: the wedding guests, the bridegroom's friends
decisions.reason: "Sons of" is a Hebrew way of speaking about people who belong to something. These are the friends who celebrate with the bridegroom.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The form of the question shows that no one would think of it.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a wedding was a time of feasting
decisions.reason: A wedding feast could last a week (Judges 14:12). Fasting belonged to mourning, so to fast at a wedding made no sense.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a picture of Jesus, recalling God as Israel's bridegroom
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God rejoicing over his people as a bridegroom over his bride (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19-20). John the Baptist calls Jesus the bridegroom (John 3:29). Jesus's presence is a time of joy.

decisions.choice: the guests at a wedding
alternatives: the sons of the bridal chamber
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom, lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, as in John 3:29. Jesus speaks of himself through the picture without naming himself.

decisions.choice: los hijos de la cámara nupcial
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom, as the English Literal does; it means the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision m1), and Balanced says so. "Hijos" here is the idiom, not a word about men, so it takes no gender span, as in Mark 2:19.

decisions.choice: l’époux (L); le marié (B, R), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:19: "l’époux" keeps the biblical picture of God as bridegroom, but today it means a husband rather than a man on his wedding day, so Balanced and Readable say "le marié". The bridegroom is a figure in the picture, so it takes no setting, as in English.

decisions.choice: wana wa ukumbi wa harusi
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek idiom, as the English Literal does; it means the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision m1), and Balanced says so. "Wana" is not limited to males, so no gender span is needed, as in Mark 2:19.

decisions.choice: "신방의 아들들" (L); "혼인 잔치의 손님들" (B); "결혼 잔치에 온 손님들" (R); "신랑" with no honorific
decisions.reason: The words of Mark 2:19 in Korean at Literal and Balanced; the bridegroom is a figure in the picture and takes no honorific, as the English uses no deity_pronoun span for him.

decisions.choice: "các con trai của phòng cưới" (L); "khách dự tiệc cưới" (B); "bạn bè của chàng rể" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:19: Literal keeps the idiom, Balanced and Readable say who is meant. "chàng rể" is lowercase and has no setting span, as in the English.

decisions.choice: Será que vocês podem ...?
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no (m2); Portuguese "Será que ...?" asks it the same way, as in Mark 2:19, without the English tag question.

decisions.choice: "विवाह-कक्ष के पुत्र" (L); "बाराती" (B); "दूल्हे के दोस्त" (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Matthew 9:15 and Mark 2:19: Literal keeps the Greek idiom; Balanced uses "बाराती", the groom's party; Readable says who they are.

decisions.choice: "молодий", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "Молодий" is the everyday Ukrainian word for the bridegroom at a wedding; "жених" is felt as Russian. The picture is of a wedding, so it stays lowercase, as in English.

decisions.choice: "婚礼の部屋の子ら" (L); "婚礼の客たち" (B); "招かれた客たち" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of the bridal chamber" is a Hebrew way of naming the bridegroom's friends, the wedding guests (m1). Literal keeps the idiom, as Mark 2:19 does in Japanese; Balanced and Readable give its meaning.

ko.R: 그러나 언젠가 신랑이 그들 곁에서 끌려갈 날이 올 것이다. 그때가 되면 그들은 금식할 것이다."

vi.L: Nhưng sẽ có những ngày đến, và khi chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ, bấy giờ họ sẽ kiêng ăn trong những ngày ấy."
vi.B: Nhưng sẽ đến những ngày chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ. Bấy giờ, trong những ngày ấy, họ sẽ kiêng ăn."
vi.R: Nhưng sẽ có ngày chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ. Lúc đó họ sẽ kiêng ăn."

pt.L: Mas virão dias, e, quando o noivo lhes for tirado, então jejuarão naqueles dias."
pt.B: Mas virão dias em que o noivo será tirado do meio deles. Então, naqueles dias, eles jejuarão."
pt.R: Mas um dia o noivo será levado para longe deles. Então, nesse tempo, eles vão jejuar."

am.L: ነገር ግን ቀኖች ይመጣሉ፤ ሙሽራውም ከእነርሱ በተወሰደ ጊዜ በዚያን ጊዜ በእነዚያ ቀኖች ይጾማሉ።»
am.B: ነገር ግን ሙሽራው ከእነርሱ የሚወሰድበት ጊዜ ይመጣል፤ በዚያን ጊዜ፣ በእነዚያ ቀኖች ይጾማሉ።»
am.R: ነገር ግን አንድ ቀን ሙሽራው ከእነርሱ ይወሰዳል። ያን ጊዜ ይጾማሉ።»

ru.L: Но придут дни, и когда будет взят от них жених, тогда будут поститься в те дни.»
ru.B: Но придут дни, когда жениха заберут у них. Тогда, в те дни, они будут поститься.»
ru.R: Но когда-нибудь жениха у них заберут. Вот тогда они будут поститься.»

hi.L: पर वे दिन आएँगे, और जब दूल्हा उनसे अलग किया जाएगा, तब उन दिनों में वे उपवास करेंगे।"
hi.B: पर ऐसे दिन आ रहे हैं जब दूल्हा उनसे छीन लिया जाएगा। तब, उन दिनों में, वे उपवास करेंगे।"
hi.R: पर एक दिन दूल्हे को उनसे दूर ले जाया जाएगा। तब, उस समय, वे उपवास करेंगे।"

uk.L: Але прийдуть дні, і коли буде взятий від них молодий, тоді вони постуватимуть у ті дні.»
uk.B: Та настануть дні, коли молодого заберуть від них. Тоді, у ті дні, вони постуватимуть.»
uk.R: Але колись молодого заберуть від них. Тоді, у той час, вони постуватимуть.»

ja.L: しかし日々が来る。そして花婿が彼らから取り去られるとき、そのとき、それらの日々に、彼らは断食するであろう。」
ja.B: しかし、花婿が彼らから取り去られる日々が来る。その日々には、彼らは断食することになる。」
ja.R: しかし、いつか、花婿が客たちのところから連れ去られる日が来る。そのとき、客たちは断食する。」

decisions.choice: the bridegroom taken away: a first hint of Jesus's death
decisions.reason: A bridegroom is not usually taken away from his own wedding. The words point ahead to Jesus being taken from his disciples (9:22). The verb may echo Isaiah 53:8, where the servant's life is taken away.

decisions.choice: days will come: a way of speaking of the future, often of trouble
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the phrase of coming sorrow (17:22; 21:6; 23:29).

decisions.choice: then they will fast: Jesus's disciples will fast after he is gone
decisions.reason: Jesus does not reject fasting; there is a time for it. The church in Acts fasts and prays (Acts 13:2-3; 14:23).

source.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying and also a parable to them that, No one a piece from a garment new having torn puts on a garment old; if but not, both the new he will tear and to the old will not match the [piece] from the new.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also told them a parable: "No one tears a piece from a new garment and puts [it] on an old garment; otherwise, [that person] will both tear the new, and the [piece] from the new will not match the old.
en.B: He told them a parable as well: "Nobody cuts a patch out of a new coat to sew on an old one. If anyone did, the new coat would be ruined, and the patch from the new would not suit the old coat either.
en.R: Jesus also told them a story to explain this. "No one cuts a piece out of new clothes to fix a hole in old clothes. If someone did that, they would ruin the new clothes. And the new piece would not look right on the old clothes.

es.L: Y les decía también una parábola: «Nadie, rasgando un pedazo de un vestido nuevo, [lo] pone sobre un vestido viejo; de lo contrario, rasgará el nuevo, y el pedazo del nuevo no concordará con el viejo.
es.B: También les contó una parábola: «Nadie corta un remiendo de un manto nuevo para coserlo en uno viejo. Si alguien lo hiciera, echaría a perder el manto nuevo, y además el remiendo del nuevo no le quedaría bien al viejo.
es.R: Jesús también les contó una historia para explicar esto: «Nadie corta un pedazo de ropa nueva para tapar un agujero en ropa vieja. Si alguien lo hiciera, estropearía la ropa nueva. Y el pedazo nuevo no se vería bien en la ropa vieja.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait aussi une parabole : « Personne ne déchire une pièce d’un vêtement neuf pour la mettre sur un vieux vêtement ; autrement, [on] déchirera le neuf, et la pièce [prise] du neuf ne s’accordera pas avec le vieux.
fr.B: Il leur dit aussi une parabole : « Personne ne découpe une pièce dans un manteau neuf pour la coudre sur un vieux manteau. Sinon, on abîmerait le manteau neuf, et la pièce prise au neuf n’irait pas non plus avec le vieux.
fr.R: Jésus leur a aussi raconté une histoire pour expliquer cela : « Personne ne découpe un morceau dans des vêtements neufs pour réparer un trou dans de vieux vêtements. Si quelqu’un faisait cela, il abîmerait les vêtements neufs. Et le morceau neuf n’irait pas bien sur les vieux vêtements.

sw.L: Alikuwa akiwaambia pia mfano: "Hakuna mtu anayechana kiraka kutoka kwenye vazi jipya na kukitia juu ya vazi kuukuu; la sivyo, atalichana lile jipya, na kiraka cha lile jipya hakitalingana na lile kuukuu.
sw.B: Aliwaambia pia mfano: "Hakuna mtu anayekata kiraka kutoka kwenye vazi jipya ili akishone juu ya vazi kuukuu. Mtu akifanya hivyo, ataharibu vazi jipya, na kiraka cha lile jipya hakitapatana na vazi kuukuu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia pia mfano ili kueleza jambo hilo. "Hakuna mtu anayekata kipande cha nguo mpya ili kuziba tundu katika nguo kuukuu. Mtu akifanya hivyo, ataiharibu nguo mpya. Tena kipande kile kipya hakitaonekana vizuri katika nguo kuukuu.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들에게 비유도 하나 말씀하셨다. "아무도 새 옷에서 조각을 찢어 내어 낡은 옷에 대고 깁지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 옷도 찢을 것이고, 새 옷에서 떼어 낸 조각도 낡은 옷에 어울리지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 또 그들에게 비유를 들어 말씀하셨다. "아무도 새 옷을 잘라 조각을 떼어 낡은 옷에 대고 깁지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 옷은 못 쓰게 되고, 새 옷에서 떼어 낸 조각도 낡은 옷과 어울리지 않는다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 이것을 설명하시려고 그들에게 비유를 하나 들어 말씀하셨다. "아무도 헌 옷에 난 구멍을 메우려고 새 옷을 잘라 내지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 옷이 망가진다. 그리고 새 옷 조각은 헌 옷과 어울리지도 않는다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng nói với họ một ngụ ngôn: "Không ai xé một miếng vá từ áo mới mà vá lên áo cũ; nếu không, [người ấy] vừa làm rách áo mới, mà miếng vá lấy từ áo mới cũng không hợp với áo cũ.
vi.B: Ngài cũng kể cho họ một ngụ ngôn: "Không ai cắt một miếng vải từ áo mới để vá vào áo cũ. Nếu làm vậy, áo mới sẽ bị hỏng, mà miếng vá lấy từ áo mới cũng không hợp với áo cũ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu còn dùng một hình ảnh so sánh để giải thích điều này: "Không ai cắt một miếng vải từ áo mới để vá chỗ rách trên áo cũ. Nếu ai làm vậy thì sẽ làm hỏng áo mới. Mà miếng vải mới vá lên áo cũ trông cũng không hợp.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} também lhes contava uma parábola: "Ninguém rasga um remendo de uma roupa nova e o põe numa roupa velha; do contrário, rasgará a nova, e o remendo tirado da nova não combinará com a velha.
pt.B: Ele também lhes contou uma parábola: "Ninguém corta um remendo de uma roupa nova para costurá-lo numa roupa velha. Se alguém fizesse isso, estragaria a roupa nova, e o remendo da nova também não combinaria com a velha.
pt.R: Jesus também contou a eles uma história para explicar isso: "Ninguém corta um pedaço de uma roupa nova para consertar um buraco numa roupa velha. Se alguém fizesse isso, estragaria a roupa nova. E o pedaço novo ficaria feio na roupa velha.

am.L: ደግሞም ምሳሌ ነገራቸው፦ «ማንም ከአዲስ ልብስ እራፊ ቀዶ በአሮጌ ልብስ ላይ አይጥፍም፤ ያለዚያ ግን አዲሱን ይቀድዳል፤ ከአዲሱም የተቀደደው እራፊ ከአሮጌው ጋር አይስማማም።
am.B: ደግሞም ይህን ምሳሌ ነገራቸው፦ «ማንም ሰው በአሮጌ ልብስ ላይ ለመጣፍ ከአዲስ ልብስ እራፊ አይቀድም። እንዲህ ቢያደርግ አዲሱን ልብስ ያበላሻል፤ ከአዲሱ የተቀደደውም እራፊ ከአሮጌው ልብስ ጋር አይስማማም።
am.R: ኢየሱስም ይህን ለማስረዳት አንድ ታሪክ ነገራቸው፦ «ማንም ሰው የአሮጌ ልብስን ቀዳዳ ለመጠገን ከአዲስ ልብስ ቁራጭ አይቆርጥም። እንዲህ ቢያደርግ አዲሱን ልብስ ያበላሻል። አዲሱም ቁራጭ በአሮጌው ልብስ ላይ ጥሩ ሆኖ አይታይም።

ru.L: Говорил же {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} им и притчу: «Никто не отрывает заплату от новой одежды и не накладывает на старую одежду; а иначе [он] и новую разорвёт, и к старой не подойдёт заплата от новой.
ru.B: Он рассказал им и притчу: «Никто не вырезает лоскут из нового плаща, чтобы пришить его к старому. Если бы кто-то так сделал, он испортил бы новый плащ, да и заплата от нового не подошла бы к старому.
ru.R: Иисус рассказал им и притчу, чтобы объяснить это: «Никто не вырезает кусок из новой одежды, чтобы залатать дыру на старой. Если кто-то так сделает, он испортит новую одежду. И новый кусок будет плохо смотреться на старой одежде.

hi.L: और उन्होंने उनसे एक दृष्टान्त भी कहा: "कोई नए वस्त्र में से टुकड़ा फाड़कर पुराने वस्त्र पर नहीं लगाता; नहीं तो [वह] नए को भी फाड़ेगा, और नए में से [लिया हुआ] टुकड़ा पुराने से मेल भी नहीं खाएगा।
hi.B: उन्होंने उन्हें एक दृष्टान्त भी सुनाया: "कोई भी नए चोग़े में से पैबंद काटकर पुराने चोग़े पर नहीं लगाता। अगर कोई ऐसा करे, तो नया चोग़ा भी बरबाद होगा, और नए का पैबंद पुराने पर ठीक भी नहीं बैठेगा।
hi.R: यीशु ने इस बात को समझाने के लिए उन्हें एक दृष्टान्त भी सुनाया। "कोई भी पुराने कपड़ों का छेद भरने के लिए नए कपड़ों में से टुकड़ा नहीं काटता। अगर कोई ऐसा करे, तो नए कपड़े ख़राब हो जाएँगे। और नया टुकड़ा पुराने कपड़ों पर ठीक भी नहीं लगेगा।

uk.L: Казав же {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} їм і притчу: «Ніхто не відриває латку від нового одягу й не накладає [її] на старий одяг; а інакше [той] і новий розірве, і латка з нового не пасуватиме до старого.
uk.B: Він розповів їм і притчу: «Ніхто не вирізає латку з нового плаща, щоб пришити її на старий. Якби хтось так зробив, то зіпсував би новий плащ, а латка з нового ще й не пасувала б до старого.
uk.R: Ісус розповів їм також притчу, щоб пояснити це. «Ніхто не вирізає шматок з нового одягу, щоб залатати дірку на старому. Якби хтось так зробив, то зіпсував би новий одяг. А новий шматок погано виглядав би на старому одязі.

ja.L: イエスはまた、彼らにたとえを話された。「だれも、新しい着物から布切れを裂き取って、古い着物に当てたりはしない。そんなことをすれば、[その人は]新しいものを裂くことになり、新しいものから取った布切れも、古いものに合わない。
ja.B: イエスはまた、彼らにたとえを話された。「だれも、新しい上着から継ぎ切れを切り取って、古い上着に縫いつけたりはしない。そんなことをすれば、新しい上着はだめになり、新しい上着から取った継ぎ切れも、古い上着には合わない。
ja.R: イエスは、このことを説明するために、たとえを話されました。「新しい服から布を切り取って、古い服の穴をつくろう人はいない。そんなことをすれば、新しい服がだめになってしまう。それに、新しい布は、古い服には似合わない。

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison taken from everyday life
decisions.reason: The word covers short sayings and pictures (4:23) as well as stories. Here Jesus gives three pictures (5:36-39).

decisions.choice: otherwise: both garments are spoiled
alternatives: only the old garment is spoiled
decisions.reason: In Luke the loss is double: the new garment is cut up, and the patch does not match the old. Mark's form of the saying speaks of the new patch pulling away from the old (Mark 2:21).

decisions.choice: the new and the old: what Jesus brings cannot be fitted into the old ways
decisions.reason: The pictures answer the question about fasting (5:33). Jesus's new work does not patch up the old customs; trying to join them spoils both.

decisions.choice: garment: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The word means a cloak worn over the tunic, a valuable piece of clothing.

decisions.choice: coat (B); clothes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: a story to explain this; to fix a hole
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a parable is here and why someone would cut a patch.

decisions.choice: [that person]
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no stated subject; Literal supplies a general one.

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); historia (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: a comparison from everyday life (meaning decision m1). Readable says "historia" where the English Readable says "story".

decisions.choice: rasgará, with no bracketed subject
decisions.reason: The English Literal supplies "[that person]". The Spanish verb ending already carries the subject, so nothing needs to be supplied. The same in verse 39.

decisions.choice: mfano (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: a comparison from everyday life (meaning decision m1). "Mfano" is also the plain word for an illustration, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "story".

decisions.choice: atalichana, with no bracketed subject
decisions.reason: The English Literal supplies "[that person]". The Swahili verb prefix already carries the subject, so nothing needs to be supplied. The same in verse 39.

decisions.choice: "비유" at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: "비유" is the word kept at every level in Korean Mark (4:2); Readable adds what it is for.

decisions.choice: "ngụ ngôn" (L, B); "hình ảnh so sánh" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled word for Jesus' parables at Literal and Balanced, as in Mark; Readable uses "hình ảnh so sánh" for a picture saying, as Mark's Readable does (3:23; 7:17).

decisions.choice: rasgará (no supplied subject)
decisions.reason: The Portuguese verb carries its subject as the Greek one does, so Literal needs no supplied "[that person]".

decisions.choice: roupa
decisions.reason: "Roupa" is the everyday word, as in Matthew 9:16 and Mark 2:21; "manto" and "veste" are bookish, and "capa" suggests a raincoat.

decisions.choice: ምሳሌ (parable, L, B); ታሪክ (story, R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "story", as the English Readable does; "ምሳሌ" is the usual word for a parable at the other levels.

decisions.choice: 'притча' at every level
decisions.reason: As settled in Matthew, a parable is 'притча' at every level; Readable adds why Jesus told it.

decisions.choice: "दृष्टान्त" at every level
decisions.reason: The book's word for parable, at every level (style guide, section 7b).
The garment is the outer cloak (meaning decision m4); "चोग़ा" names a long outer robe, where "कोट" would be a modern jacket.

decisions.choice: "притча" at every level
decisions.reason: The Gospel convention keeps "притча" at every level; Readable adds "щоб пояснити це" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "たとえ" (every level)
decisions.reason: The word covers short pictures as well as stories (m1). Japanese says "たとえ" at every level, as the shared Gospel terms set; Readable adds why Jesus told it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·

records.literal_gloss: And no one puts wine new into wineskins old; if but not, will burst the wine the new the wineskins, and it will be spilled out and the wineskins will be destroyed;

en.L: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled out, and the wineskins will be destroyed.
en.B: Nor does anyone store new wine in old wineskins. That would make the skins split open; the new wine would spill, and the skins would be lost.
en.R: And no one puts new wine into old bags made of skin. The new wine would make the old skins break open. The wine would pour out, and the skins would be no good anymore.

es.L: Y nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos; de lo contrario, el vino nuevo reventará los odres, y él se derramará, y los odres se echarán a perder.
es.B: Tampoco nadie guarda vino nuevo en odres viejos. Eso haría que los odres se rajaran: el vino nuevo se derramaría y los odres se perderían.
es.R: Y nadie pone vino nuevo en bolsas de cuero viejas. El vino nuevo haría reventar los cueros viejos. El vino se saldría, y los cueros ya no servirían para nada.

fr.L: Et personne ne met du vin nouveau dans de vieilles outres ; autrement, le vin nouveau fera éclater les outres, et il se répandra, et les outres seront perdues.
fr.B: Personne non plus ne verse du vin nouveau dans de vieilles outres. Le vin ferait éclater les outres ; il se répandrait, et les outres seraient perdues.
fr.R: Et personne ne met du vin nouveau dans de vieux sacs en peau de bête. Le vin nouveau ferait éclater les vieux sacs. Le vin coulerait par terre, et les sacs ne serviraient plus à rien.

sw.L: Na hakuna mtu anayetia divai mpya katika viriba vikuukuu; la sivyo, divai mpya itavipasua viriba, nayo itamwagika, na viriba vitaharibika.
sw.B: Wala hakuna mtu anayehifadhi divai mpya katika viriba vikuukuu. Hiyo ingefanya viriba vipasuke; divai mpya ingemwagika, na viriba vingeharibika.
sw.R: Na hakuna mtu anayeweka divai mpya katika mifuko mikuukuu ya ngozi. Divai mpya ingeipasua ile mifuko mikuukuu. Divai ingemwagika, na mifuko isingefaa tena.

ko.L: 그리고 아무도 새 포도주를 낡은 가죽 부대에 넣지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 포도주가 가죽 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주는 쏟아지고 가죽 부대는 못 쓰게 될 것이다.
ko.B: 또 아무도 새 포도주를 낡은 가죽 부대에 담지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 포도주가 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주는 쏟아지고 부대는 버리게 된다.
ko.R: 또 사람들은 새 포도주를 짐승 가죽으로 만든 낡은 부대에 담지 않는다. 새 포도주가 낡은 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주도 쏟아지고 부대도 못 쓰게 되기 때문이다.

vi.L: Và không ai đổ rượu mới vào bầu da cũ; nếu không, rượu mới sẽ làm nứt bầu, và rượu sẽ đổ ra, và bầu sẽ hư mất.
vi.B: Cũng không ai đổ rượu mới vào bầu da cũ. Nếu làm vậy, rượu mới sẽ làm bục bầu da; rượu sẽ đổ ra, và bầu cũng hư mất.
vi.R: Cũng không ai đổ rượu mới vào túi da cũ. Rượu mới sẽ làm túi da cũ bị nứt vỡ. Rượu sẽ chảy ra hết, và túi da cũng không dùng được nữa.

pt.L: E ninguém põe vinho novo em odres velhos; do contrário, o vinho novo romperá os odres, e ele se derramará, e os odres se perderão.
pt.B: Também ninguém guarda vinho novo em odres velhos. Os odres se rachariam, o vinho novo se derramaria, e os odres se perderiam.
pt.R: E ninguém põe vinho novo em sacos velhos de couro. O vinho novo faria os sacos velhos estourarem. O vinho se derramaria, e os sacos não serviriam mais para nada.

am.L: ማንም አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ በአሮጌ አቁማዳ ውስጥ አያደርግም፤ ያለዚያ ግን አዲሱ የወይን ጠጅ አቁማዳዎቹን ይቀድዳል፤ እርሱም ይፈሳል፤ አቁማዳዎቹም ይጠፋሉ።
am.B: እንዲሁም ማንም አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ በአሮጌ አቁማዳ ውስጥ አያስቀምጥም። ቢያስቀምጥ አቁማዳዎቹ ይቀደዳሉ፤ አዲሱ የወይን ጠጅ ይፈሳል፤ አቁማዳዎቹም ይበላሻሉ።
am.R: ማንም ሰው አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ ከቆዳ በተሠራ አሮጌ ዕቃ ውስጥ አያስቀምጥም። አዲሱ የወይን ጠጅ አሮጌውን የቆዳ ዕቃ ይቀድደዋል። የወይን ጠጁ ይፈሳል፤ የቆዳ ዕቃዎቹም ከጥቅም ውጭ ይሆናሉ።

ru.L: И никто не наливает молодое вино в старые мехи; а иначе молодое вино прорвёт мехи, и само вытечет, и мехи пропадут.
ru.B: И никто не наливает молодое вино в старые мехи. Иначе вино разорвёт мехи, само выльется, и мехи пропадут.
ru.R: И никто не наливает молодое вино в старые кожаные мешки. Молодое вино разорвёт старые мехи. Вино выльется, а мехи больше ни на что не будут годиться.

hi.L: और कोई नया दाखरस पुरानी मशकों में नहीं भरता; नहीं तो नया दाखरस मशकों को फाड़ देगा, और वह बह जाएगा, और मशकें नष्ट हो जाएँगी।
hi.B: और न कोई नया दाखरस पुरानी मशकों में रखता है। ऐसा करने से मशकें फट जाएँगी; नया दाखरस बह जाएगा, और मशकें भी बरबाद हो जाएँगी।
hi.R: और कोई नया दाखरस चमड़े के पुराने थैलों में नहीं भरता। नया दाखरस पुराने थैलों को फाड़ देगा। दाखरस बह जाएगा, और थैले भी किसी काम के नहीं रहेंगे।

uk.L: І ніхто не вливає молодого вина в старі бурдюки; а інакше молоде вино розірве бурдюки, і само виллється, і бурдюки пропадуть.
uk.B: І ніхто не наливає молодого вина в старі бурдюки. Від цього шкіра порветься: молоде вино розіллється, і бурдюки пропадуть.
uk.R: І ніхто не наливає молодого вина в старі шкіряні міхи. Молоде вино розірвало б старі міхи. Вино вилилося б, а міхи вже ні на що не годилися б.

ja.L: また、だれも、新しいぶどう酒を古い革袋に入れたりはしない。そんなことをすれば、新しいぶどう酒は革袋を裂き、ぶどう酒そのものも流れ出て、革袋もだめになる。
ja.B: また、だれも新しいぶどう酒を古い革袋に入れたりはしない。そんなことをすれば、革袋は裂けて、新しいぶどう酒は流れ出し、革袋もだめになってしまう。
ja.R: また、新しいぶどう酒を、動物の皮で作った古い袋に入れる人はいない。そんなことをすれば、新しいぶどう酒が古い袋を破ってしまう。ぶどう酒は流れ出て、袋はもう使えなくなる。

decisions.choice: new wine in old wineskins: fermenting wine stretches the skin
decisions.reason: Wine was kept in bags made from whole goat skins. New wine was still fermenting and gave off gas. A new skin could stretch; an old one was dry and stiff, and would split.

decisions.choice: bags made of skin
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

decisions.choice: "bầu da" (L, B); "túi da" (R) for wineskins
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:22.

decisions.choice: odres (L, B); sacos de couro (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 9:17 and Mark 2:22: "odre" is the right word but unknown to many young readers, so Readable says what it was.

decisions.choice: አቁማዳ (wineskins, L, B); ከቆዳ የተሠራ ዕቃ, የቆዳ ዕቃ (a container made of skin, R)
decisions.reason: The Amharic word for a skin bag is kept, as in Matthew 9:17; Readable says what it is made of, so the bursting makes sense.

decisions.choice: 'молодое вино'; 'мехи' (R adds 'кожаные мешки')
decisions.reason: As in Mark 2:22, the wine is 'молодое', still fermenting; Readable explains the wineskins once.

decisions.choice: "मशकें" (L, B); "चमड़े के थैले" (R)
decisions.reason: "मशक" is the Hindi word for a leather water or wine bag; Readable describes it, as in Matthew 9:17 and Mark 2:22.

decisions.choice: "молоде вино"; "бурдюки" (L, B); "шкіряні міхи" (R)
decisions.reason: "Молоде вино" is the Ukrainian for wine still fermenting, which is the point of the picture; Readable says plainly that the containers were made of skin.

source.text: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.

records.literal_gloss: But wine new into wineskins fresh must be put.

en.L: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
en.B: Instead, new wine has to be put into fresh skins.
en.R: New wine must go into new skins.

es.L: Sino que el vino nuevo debe echarse en odres sin usar.
es.B: Al contrario, el vino nuevo hay que ponerlo en odres sin estrenar.
es.R: El vino nuevo debe ir en cueros nuevos.

fr.L: Mais le vin nouveau doit être mis dans des outres neuves.
fr.B: Au contraire, le vin nouveau doit être mis dans des outres neuves.
fr.R: Le vin nouveau, il faut le mettre dans des sacs neufs.

sw.L: Bali divai mpya inapasa kutiwa katika viriba visivyotumika.
sw.B: Badala yake, divai mpya lazima iwekwe katika viriba ambavyo havijatumika.
sw.R: Divai mpya inapaswa kuwekwa katika mifuko mipya ya ngozi.

ko.L: 오히려 새 포도주는 새 가죽 부대에 넣어야 한다.
ko.B: 새 포도주는 새 부대에 담아야 한다.
ko.R: 새 포도주는 새 부대에 담아야 한다.

vi.L: Nhưng rượu mới phải được đổ vào bầu da còn mới.
vi.B: Rượu mới phải được đựng trong bầu da còn mới.
vi.R: Rượu mới phải được đổ vào túi da mới.

pt.L: Mas vinho novo deve ser posto em odres ainda não usados.
pt.B: Pelo contrário, vinho novo tem de ser posto em odres que nunca foram usados.
pt.R: Vinho novo tem de ser posto em sacos novos.

am.L: ነገር ግን አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ ገና ባልተሠራበት አቁማዳ ውስጥ መደረግ አለበት።
am.B: ይልቁንም አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ ገና ባልተሠራበት አቁማዳ ውስጥ መጨመር አለበት።
am.R: አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ በአዲስ የቆዳ ዕቃ ውስጥ መቀመጥ አለበት።

ru.L: Но молодое вино должно вливать в новые мехи.
ru.B: Молодое вино нужно наливать в новые мехи.
ru.R: Молодому вину нужны новые мехи.

hi.L: पर नया दाखरस कोरी मशकों में भरना चाहिए।
hi.B: बल्कि नए दाखरस को कोरी मशकों में भरना चाहिए।
hi.R: नया दाखरस नए थैलों में ही भरना चाहिए।

uk.L: Але молоде вино треба вливати в нові бурдюки.
uk.B: Молоде вино треба наливати в нові бурдюки.
uk.R: Молоде вино треба наливати в нові міхи.

ja.L: むしろ、新しいぶどう酒は、まだ使われていない革袋に入れなければならない。
ja.B: 新しいぶどう酒は、使ったことのない革袋に入れなければならない。
ja.R: 新しいぶどう酒は、新しい袋に入れなければならない。

decisions.choice: the sentence ends here, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "and both are kept safe" added, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts end with "must be put". Many later ones add words found in Matthew 9:17. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: new wine, fresh wineskins: two different words for new
decisions.reason: The word used for the wine means recently made; the word used for the skins (and for the garment in 5:36) means not yet used.

decisions.choice: fresh (L, B); new (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the two Greek words apart; Readable uses the plainer word.

decisions.choice: odres sin usar (L); odres sin estrenar (B); cueros nuevos (R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses two different words for "new" (meaning decision m2): the wine is newly made, the skins are fresh, never used. Spanish has one ordinary word, so Literal and Balanced say "not yet used" for the skins, as the English "fresh" does.

decisions.choice: vin nouveau, outres neuves
decisions.reason: The Greek has two words for new (m2). French "nouveau" (recently made) and "neuf" (not yet used) already keep them apart, so no rarer word is needed; "fraîches" would suggest cool skins.

decisions.choice: visivyotumika (L); ambavyo havijatumika (B); mipya (R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses two different words for "new" (meaning decision m2): the wine is newly made, the skins are fresh, never used. Swahili "-pya" covers both, so Literal and Balanced say "not yet used" for the skins, as the English "fresh" does.

decisions.choice: "새" for both neos and kainos
decisions.reason: Korean has no pair of everyday words that keeps the difference without strain; the meaning decision records it.

decisions.choice: "rượu mới" but "bầu da còn mới" (L, B); "túi da mới" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes two Greek words for "new": the wine is newly made, the skins unused. "còn mới" (still new, not yet used) keeps the difference at Literal and Balanced, as the English "fresh" does.

decisions.choice: ainda não usados (L); que nunca foram usados (B); novos (R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese has one everyday word, "novo", for both Greek words (m2). Literal and Balanced say what the second one means, not yet used, so that the two stay apart; Readable says "novos", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ገና ያልተሠራበት አቁማዳ (a skin not yet used, L, B) beside አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ (new wine)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two different words for new: young wine, and skins that are fresh and unused. Literal and Balanced keep them apart; Readable says "new" for both, as the English does.
The Greek has two words for new (meaning decision m2): the wine is newly made, the skins unused. "कोरी" means fresh, never used, and keeps the two apart; Readable says "new", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "新しいぶどう酒", "まだ使われていない革袋" (L), "使ったことのない革袋" (B); "新しい袋" (R)
decisions.reason: Greek uses two words for new: recently made for the wine, not yet used for the skins (m2). Literal and Balanced keep them apart, as the English does with "fresh"; Readable uses the plain word.

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And no one having drunk old desires new; he says for, The old good is.

en.L: And no one who has drunk old [wine] wants new, for [that person] says, 'The old is good.'"
en.B: And nobody who has been drinking old wine wants the new. 'The old is good,' they say."
en.R: And people who have been drinking old wine do not want new wine. They say, 'The old wine is good.'"

es.L: Y nadie que ha bebido [vino] añejo quiere nuevo, porque dice: “El añejo es bueno”».
es.B: Y nadie que haya estado bebiendo vino añejo quiere el nuevo. “El añejo es bueno”, dice».
es.R: Y la gente que ha estado bebiendo vino añejo no quiere vino nuevo. Dicen: “El vino añejo es bueno”».

fr.L: Et personne, ayant bu du vieux, ne veut du nouveau, car [on] dit : “Le vieux est bon.” »
fr.B: Et personne, après avoir bu du vin vieux, ne veut du nouveau : “Le vieux est bon”, dit-on. »
fr.R: Et les gens qui ont l’habitude de boire du vin vieux ne veulent pas de vin nouveau. Ils disent : “Le vin vieux est bon.” »

sw.L: Na hakuna mtu aliyekunywa [divai] ya zamani anayetaka mpya; kwa maana husema, 'Ya zamani ni nzuri.'"
sw.B: Na hakuna mtu ambaye amekuwa akinywa divai ya zamani anayetaka mpya. Husema, 'Ya zamani ni nzuri.'"
sw.R: Na watu ambao wamekuwa wakinywa divai ya zamani hawataki divai mpya. Wao husema, 'Divai ya zamani ni nzuri.'"

ko.L: 그리고 묵은 [포도주를] 마신 사람은 아무도 새 [포도주를] 원하지 않는다. 그가 '묵은 것이 좋다'고 말하기 때문이다."
ko.B: 그리고 묵은 포도주를 마셔 본 사람은 아무도 새것을 원하지 않는다. '묵은 것이 좋다' 하고 말하기 때문이다."
ko.R: 그리고 묵은 포도주를 마시던 사람은 새 포도주를 마시고 싶어 하지 않는다. 그들은 '묵은 포도주가 좋다'고 말한다."

vi.L: Và không ai đã uống [rượu] cũ lại muốn [rượu] mới; vì [người ấy] nói: '[Rượu] cũ thì ngon.'"
vi.B: Cũng không ai đã uống rượu cũ mà lại muốn rượu mới. Họ nói: 'Rượu cũ ngon.'"
vi.R: Người nào đã uống rượu cũ thì không muốn uống rượu mới. Họ nói: 'Rượu cũ ngon lắm.'"

pt.L: E ninguém que bebeu [vinho] velho quer o novo, pois diz: 'O velho é bom.'"
pt.B: E ninguém que esteve bebendo vinho velho quer o novo. 'O velho é bom', dizem."
pt.R: E as pessoas que estão bebendo vinho velho não querem vinho novo. Elas dizem: 'O vinho velho é bom.'"

am.L: አሮጌውንም የጠጣ ማንም አዲሱን አይፈልግም፤ “አሮጌው መልካም ነው” ይላልና።»
am.B: አሮጌውን የወይን ጠጅ ሲጠጣ የቆየ ማንም አዲሱን አይፈልግም። “አሮጌው ጥሩ ነው” ይላል።»
am.R: አሮጌ የወይን ጠጅ ሲጠጡ የኖሩ ሰዎች አዲሱን አይፈልጉም። “አሮጌው የወይን ጠጅ ጥሩ ነው” ይላሉ።»

ru.L: И никто, выпив старого, не хочет молодого, ведь [он] говорит: “Старое хорошее.”»
ru.B: И никто, выпив старого вина, не хочет молодого. “Старое хорошее”, — говорят люди.»
ru.R: И кто пил старое вино, тот не хочет молодого. Люди говорят: “Старое вино хорошее.”»

hi.L: और कोई पुराना [दाखरस] पीकर नया नहीं चाहता, क्योंकि [वह] कहता है, 'पुराना अच्छा है।'"
hi.B: और जो कोई पुराना दाखरस पीता रहा हो, वह नया नहीं चाहता। 'पुराना ही अच्छा है,' वह कहता है।"
hi.R: और जो लोग पुराना दाखरस पीते आए हैं, वे नया दाखरस नहीं चाहते। वे कहते हैं, 'पुराना दाखरस ही अच्छा है।'"

uk.L: І ніхто, напившись старого, не хоче молодого, бо каже: “Старе добре.”»
uk.B: І ніхто, хто пив старе вино, не хоче молодого. “Старе добре”, — кажуть вони.»
uk.R: І ті, хто пʼє старе вино, не хочуть молодого. Вони кажуть: “Старе вино добре.”»

ja.L: また、古い[ぶどう酒]を飲んだ者は、だれも新しいものを望まない。『古いものは良い』と[その人は]言うからである。」
ja.B: また、古いぶどう酒を飲んでいる人は、だれも新しいものを欲しがらない。『古いのが良い』と言うのだ。」
ja.R: また、古いぶどう酒を飲みなれた人は、新しいぶどう酒を欲しがらない。『古いぶどう酒がおいしい』と言うのだ。」

decisions.choice: good, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: better, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have "good"; many later ones have "better". With "good", the drinker is content with the old and does not want to try the new. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the verse belongs to the text, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse left out, as in a few early witnesses
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, among them Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, leave out the verse; the rest have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one who has drunk old wine wants new: people content with the old do not look for the new
alternatives: old wine is better than new
decisions.reason: The saying closes the pictures with a comment on people: many who are used to the old ways will not welcome what Jesus brings.

decisions.choice: [that person] (L); they (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; the person is anyone who has drunk old wine.

decisions.choice: añejo
decisions.reason: "Añejo" is the Spanish word for wine that has aged and is valued for it, which is the point of the saying (meaning decision m3); "vino viejo" sounds spoiled.

decisions.choice: "묵은" for old wine, against "낡은" for the old wineskins (5:37)
decisions.reason: Korean uses "묵은" for aged wine; "낡은" would say it had gone bad.

decisions.choice: "ngon" for good
decisions.reason: Said of wine, the word means pleasant to drink; "ngon hơn" would follow the reading the SBLGNT does not have (meaning decision).
